patch.value: Retire the bespoke gate scripts onto the assurance primitives, with a recorded per-script disposition so 6,500 lines of external enforcement either moves into the product or says why it cannot

This repository is the first and hardest adopter. 16 files matching *gate*.mjs carry 6,500 LOC and 20 scripts drive the pm CLI as a subprocess. Each one is a candidate for a declaration, and the ones that are not are the interesting cases: a gate that verifies a published npm artifact or drives a real installation is exercising the world rather than measuring the record, and it should stay a script that reports a provider measurement rather than pretend to be one. The output of this work is a ledger with one row per script: migrated (with the declaration ids that replaced it), reduced to a provider, or retained with a reason. Migration is only complete when the retained set is smaller than the migrated set and every retained script's reason names something the record genuinely cannot answer. Doing this in this repository is what proves the primitives are sufficient rather than merely plausible, and it is also the fastest way to find out which parts of the vocabulary are missing, because every script that resists migration is naming a gap. Sequence after the primitives land; each migration lands with the negative control the assertion requires, so the migrated bound is proven to be able to fail before the script it replaces is deleted.

A ledger records every gate script with a disposition of migrated, reduced to provider, or retained with a reason naming what the record cannot answer; Every migrated bound lands with a proven negative control before the script it replaces is removed; The migrated set is larger than the retained set, and total gate LOC outside the product falls measurably; The release pipeline runs the native gates and the retained scripts through one declared inventory rather than two parallel mechanisms

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Adoption baseline measured 2026-08-11, immediately after the assurance primitives shipped in 2026.8.11.

The capability is complete. pm-2lex4r (measure), pm-lyfu7b (assert), pm-wn6wot (gate) and pm-91xeam (verdicts) are all closed, pm assurance exposes list, show, put, remove, run and verdicts, and docs/ASSURANCE.md documents nine measurement sources, seven assertion polarities, three scopes, two lifetimes and three enforcement levels.

Nothing uses it.

- pm assurance list measurement, list assertion and list gate all return count 0.
- .agents/pm/assurance.json does not exist.
- grep for assurance across .github/workflows/ and scripts/ returns one incidental hit in a token baseline JSON file and no invocation.

Meanwhile the enforcement the project actually relies on is still declared elsewhere: scripts/release/tracker-measurements.json holds 30 declarations across five selector sources (health_check 10, dependency_kind 6, graph_finding 5, graph_profile 4, validate_warning 5), and the only reader is scripts/release/tracker-measurement-gate.mjs.

So the project now has two enforcement vocabularies. The one that ships inside the product has zero members and zero consumers. The one that gates every release lives in a script this item exists to retire. That is the same producer-and-consumer asymmetry recorded as roadmap horizon AG, applied to the mechanism that was built to end it.

This is the starting state for the per-script disposition this item owns, and it is also why the disposition should be written as declarations rather than as prose: every row of tracker-measurements.json that has an equivalent assurance source can be expressed today, and each one that cannot names a genuine provider gap for pm-uhv1m5.

author: harness:claude-code
message: Raise to P1: the assurance registry shipped with zero declarations and zero CI consumers, so the migration this item owns is now the binding constraint on enforcement

value.note: quality:static now runs the product's own assurance gates in CI, closing the zero-consumer half of this migration
